sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的DealBook峰会上，现场采访商业、政治和文化领域一些最有影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilron Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔隆·蒙达尼以及其他许多人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at NYTimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在NYTimes.com上直播部分精选采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅用户，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: My name is Irina Alexander, and I'm a contributing writer to The New York Times magazine.
sentences.zh: 我叫伊琳娜·亚历山大，是《纽约时报》杂志的特约撰稿人。

sentences.en: A few weeks ago, I had a story on the cover of the magazine about the collapse of the fashion industry.
sentences.zh: 几周前，我在杂志封面上发表了一篇关于时尚产业崩溃的报道。

sentences.en: In April, I was sitting at home, I was bored, and my editor and I were on the phone, and she said, you know, well, what's happening with the fashion industry right now?
sentences.zh: 四月份的时候，我坐在家里，感到很无聊，我和编辑通了电话，她说，你知道，时尚产业现在到底发生了什么？

sentences.en: Because we saw these other industries, like restaurants and everybody else, the film industry was struggling.
sentences.zh: 因为我们看到其他行业，比如餐饮业和其他所有行业，电影业都在苦苦挣扎。

sentences.en: And I said, well, actually, I have no idea what's happening in fashion.
sentences.zh: 我说，其实我也不知道时尚界发生了什么。

sentences.en: I mean, I feel like everyone's wearing sweatpants, but I said, you know, I met this guy about a year ago
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我觉得每个人都在穿运动裤，但我说，你知道，我大约一年前认识了一个人，

sentences.en: who used to design Band of Outsiders, who was Scott Sternberg, and I said, let me reach out to him and see if maybe he knows what's happening in the fashion industry.
sentences.zh: 他曾经设计过“局外人乐队”（Band of Outsiders），他叫斯科特·斯特恩伯格，我说，让我联系一下他，看看他是否知道时尚界正在发生什么。

sentences.en: And Scott and I happen to live in the same neighborhood in Los Angeles, so every day I was trying to find, like, destinations I could walk to to just, like, get out of my house.
sentences.zh: 我和斯科特恰好住在洛杉矶的同一个社区，所以我每天都在找我可以步行到达的目的地，只是为了离开家。

sentences.en: And one day I walked to his house, and I sort of very casually asked him what's happening in the fashion industry.
sentences.zh: 有一天我走到他家，很随意地问他时尚界发生了什么。

sentences.en: The minute he started talking, I realized that the story was so much bigger than I had anticipated.
sentences.zh: 他刚开始说，我就意识到这个故事比我预想的要大得多。

sentences.en: I'd been covering the fashion industry on and off for about a decade.
sentences.zh: 我断断续续报道时尚产业大约十年了。

sentences.en: And I knew that the industry had been in trouble long before the pandemic, but I didn't realize just how bad it had been
sentences.zh: 我知道这个行业在疫情爆发前很久就陷入了困境，但我没有意识到情况有多糟糕，

sentences.en: and how there had been this ginormous bubble of overproduction with too many shows and too many collections and too many clothes
sentences.zh: 以及这里曾存在一个巨大的产能过剩泡沫，有太多的时装秀、太多的系列和太多的衣服，

sentences.en: and a sort of set of people who had acted so irresponsibly in a way that really kind of drove the industry into the ground.
sentences.zh: 还有一群人以一种真正把这个行业推向深渊的方式行事，极其不负责任。

sentences.en: It really reminded me of 2008 and the financial crash.
sentences.zh: 这真的让我想起了2008年的金融危机。

sentences.en: And I thought, what if you tried to write about the fashion industry the way you would any other bubble,
sentences.zh: 我想，如果你试着像报道其他任何泡沫一样去报道时尚产业，会怎样呢？

sentences.en: like the subprime mortgage crisis, and really got into what happened to the industry on a really granular level.
sentences.zh: 比如次贷危机，真正深入到这个行业到底发生了什么，从非常细致的层面去剖析。

sentences.en: So here's my story called Sweatpants Forever, read by Julia Whelan.
sentences.zh: 这就是我的故事《永远的运动裤》，由朱莉娅·惠兰朗读。

sentences.en: It's difficult, in retrospect, to pinpoint when exactly panic about coronavirus took hold in the United States, but March 12th stands out.
sentences.zh: 回想起来，很难确定人们对冠状病毒的恐慌究竟是何时在美国蔓延开来的，但3月12日是一个突出的节点。

sentences.en: Stores ran out of canned goods.
sentences.zh: 商店里的罐头食品被抢购一空。

sentences.en: Streets emptied of cars.
sentences.zh: 街道上空无一车。

sentences.en: Tom Hanks had just tested positive for the virus.
sentences.zh: 汤姆·汉克斯刚刚被检测出病毒呈阳性。

sentences.en: That evening, Scott Sternberg, a fashion designer, was lying awake at home in the Silver Lake neighborhood of Los Angeles,
sentences.zh: 那天晚上，时装设计师斯科特·斯特恩伯格躺在洛杉矶银湖社区的家中，彻夜难眠，

sentences.en: thinking about Entire World, a line of basics he founded two years earlier.
sentences.zh: 想着他两年前创立的基础服装品牌Entire World。

sentences.en: Would people still buy clothes?
sentences.zh: 人们还会买衣服吗？

sentences.en: How much cash did he have to keep going?
sentences.zh: 他还有多少现金可以维持运营？

sentences.en: When would he have to lay people off?
sentences.zh: 他什么时候必须裁员？

sentences.en: My band of outsiders battle scars just opened wide, he said.
sentences.zh: “我‘局外人乐队’时期的伤疤又裂开了，”他说。

sentences.en: Band of Outsiders was Sternberg's previous company.
sentences.zh: “局外人乐队”是斯特恩伯格之前的公司。

sentences.en: He founded it in 2004 as a line of slim shirts and ties.
sentences.zh: 他于2004年创立了它，主打修身衬衫和领带。

sentences.en: Remember the skinny tie boom?
sentences.zh: 还记得窄领带热潮吗？

sentences.en: That was Sternberg.
sentences.zh: 那就是斯特恩伯格带起来的。

sentences.en: Eventually, it grew into full men's and women's collections that won over the fashion world with self-consciously preppy clothes.
sentences.zh: 最终，它发展成了完整的男装和女装系列，以刻意营造的学院风服装赢得了时尚界的青睐。

sentences.en: Sternberg took home two Council of Fashion Designers of America, CFDA, awards, the industry's equivalent of the Oscars.
sentences.zh: 斯特恩伯格获得了两项美国时装设计师协会（CFDA）大奖，这相当于时尚界的奥斯卡奖。

sentences.en: He posed for photos with Kanye WeSt.
sentences.zh: 他曾与坎耶·韦斯特合影。

sentences.en: Michelle Obama wore one of his dresses.
sentences.zh: 米歇尔·奥巴马穿过他设计的一件裙子。

sentences.en: He opened stores in Tokyo and New York.
sentences.zh: 他在东京和纽约开了店。

sentences.en: Then, in 2015, to everyone's surprise,
sentences.zh: 然后，在2015年，令所有人惊讶的是，

sentences.en: Sternberg announced that Band was going out of business.
sentences.zh: 斯特恩伯格宣布“局外人乐队”倒闭了。

sentences.en: An investment with some Belgians had gone bad, but that didn't feel like the whole story.
sentences.zh: 与一些比利时人的投资出了问题，但这似乎并不是故事的全部。

sentences.en: Sternberg knew the whole story.
sentences.zh: 斯特恩伯格知道全部真相。

sentences.en: Every choice he made at Entire World was to prevent it from happening again.
sentences.zh: 他在Entire World所做的每一个选择，都是为了防止同样的事情再次发生。

sentences.en: Now, a global pandemic had hit.
sentences.zh: 现在，一场全球性的大流行病袭来了。

sentences.en: He couldn't foresee that.
sentences.zh: 他无法预见这一点。

sentences.en: No one did.
sentences.zh: 没有人能预见。

sentences.en: Unlike other designers, Sternberg studied not design, but economics, a major he chose in part because the year he entered Washington University in St. Louis,
sentences.zh: 与其他设计师不同，斯特恩伯格学的不是设计，而是经济学，他选择这个专业的部分原因是，在他进入圣路易斯华盛顿大学的那一年，

sentences.en: the economist Douglas North, a professor there, won a Nobel Prize.
sentences.zh: 在那任教的经济学家道格拉斯·诺斯获得了诺贝尔奖。

sentences.en: Sternberg graduated summa cum laude.
sentences.zh: 斯特恩伯格以最优等成绩毕业。

sentences.en: His senior thesis was about the economics of actors in Hollywood, which is how he wound up in Los Angeles in the first place.
sentences.zh: 他的毕业论文是关于好莱坞演员的经济学，这也是他最终来到洛杉矶的原因。

sentences.en: This is all to say that Sternberg knew what uncertainty does to consumer behavior.
sentences.zh: 这一切都是为了说明，斯特恩伯格知道不确定性会对消费者行为产生什么影响。

sentences.en: What was going through my head was, man, I don't know how big businesses are going to deal with this, he said.
sentences.zh: “我当时脑子里想的是，天哪，我不知道大企业将如何应对这种情况，”他说。

sentences.en: But for a small business, this is enough to take all of us out, he snapped his fingers, in one shot.
sentences.zh: “但对于小企业来说，这足以让我们所有人，”他打了个响指，“一下子全完蛋。”

sentences.en: As it happened, it was the Giants who would fall firSt.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，首先倒下的正是那些巨头。

sentences.en: Over the next few months, J.Crew, Neiman Marcus, Brooks Brothers, and J.C.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的几个月里，J.Crew、内曼·马库斯、布克兄弟和杰西潘尼（J.C. Penney）

sentences.en: Penney filed for bankruptcy.
sentences.zh: 申请了破产保护。

sentences.en: Gap, Inc.
sentences.zh: 盖璞（Gap, Inc.）

sentences.en: couldn't pay rent on its 2,785 North American stores.
sentences.zh: 无法支付其在北美2785家门店的租金。

sentences.en: By July, Diane von Furstenberg announced she would lay off 300 employees and close 18 of her 19 stores.
sentences.zh: 到了七月，黛安·冯芙丝汀宝宣布将裁员300人，并关闭其19家门店中的18家。

sentences.en: The impending damage to small businesses was inconceivable.
sentences.zh: 对小企业即将造成的损害是不可想象的。

sentences.en: The next morning, a Friday, Sternberg drove to entire world offices in Koreatown.
sentences.zh: 第二天早上，一个周五，斯特恩伯格开车去了位于韩国城的Entire World办公室。

sentences.en: He sat down at his desk and began drafting an email.
sentences.zh: 他坐在办公桌前，开始起草一封电子邮件。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: I mean, WTF.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，搞什么鬼（WTF）。

sentences.en: He didn't run the email by his staff.
sentences.zh: 他没有让员工过目这封邮件。

sentences.en: There was no meeting about it.
sentences.zh: 没有为此召开会议。

sentences.en: He just sat down and wrote it.
sentences.zh: 他只是坐下来写了它。

sentences.en: Am I sick already?
sentences.zh: 我已经生病了吗？

sentences.en: Can I leave my house?
sentences.zh: 我可以离开家吗？

sentences.en: What do I tell my employees?
sentences.zh: 我该怎么告诉我的员工？

sentences.en: Will my mom be okay on her flight home today?
sentences.zh: 我妈妈今天回家的航班会平安吗？

sentences.en: Can Zod, Sternberg's dog, get coronavirus?
sentences.zh: 佐德（斯特恩伯格的狗）会感染冠状病毒吗？

sentences.en: Did I buy enough TP?
sentences.zh: 我买够卫生纸了吗？

sentences.en: How long will this last?
sentences.zh: 这会持续多久？

sentences.en: Who's in charge?
sentences.zh: 谁负责？

sentences.en: What's next?
sentences.zh: 接下来会发生什么？

sentences.en: The email went out to the brand's 30,000 subscribers on Sunday, March 15th.
sentences.zh: 这封邮件于3月15日星期日发送给了该品牌的3万名订阅者。

sentences.en: It was, in a sea of daily promotional emails, a distinctly human one.
sentences.zh: 在每天铺天盖地的促销邮件中，这是一封充满人情味的邮件。

sentences.en: But this was still a promotion.
sentences.zh: 但这仍然是一次促销。

sentences.en: For a sweatsuit, the brand's top seller.
sentences.zh: 针对的是该品牌的畅销产品——运动套装。

sentences.en: A hero item in industry speak.
sentences.zh: 用业内的话说，这是一款“英雄单品”。

sentences.en: Inspired by a French children's film, entire world sweatsuits come in a prism of cheery colors.
sentences.zh: 受一部法国儿童电影的启发，Entire World的运动套装有各种欢快的颜色。

sentences.en: And in Sternberg's vision, sort of make you look like a cross between a Teletubby, Ben Stiller in the Royal Tenenbaums, and a JCPenney ad from 1979.
sentences.zh: 按照斯特恩伯格的构想，穿上它让你看起来像是天线宝宝、电影《天才一族》里的本·斯蒂勒，以及1979年杰西潘尼广告的结合体。

sentences.en: It wasn't long before Sternberg's employees began texting him happy face emoji.
sentences.zh: 没过多久，斯特恩伯格的员工就开始给他发笑脸表情符号了。

sentences.en: On an average day, the brand, still in its nascent stage, sells 46 sweats.
sentences.zh: 在平时，这个尚处于起步阶段的品牌每天能卖出46套运动服。

sentences.en: That day, they sold more than a thousand.
sentences.zh: 那天，他们卖出了超过一千套。

sentences.en: When they ran out of sweatsuits, shoppers moved through the T-shirts, socks, and underwear.
sentences.zh: 当运动套装卖光时，顾客开始购买T恤、袜子和内衣。

sentences.en: By month's end, the brand's sales were up 662% over March the previous year.
sentences.zh: 到月底，该品牌的销售额比去年三月增长了662%。

sentences.en: The day we met, April 24th, was the highest grossing day in the company's history.
sentences.zh: 我们见面的那天，即4月24日，是公司历史上销售额最高的一天。

sentences.en: A new shipment came in that morning and promptly sold out again.
sentences.zh: 那天早上新到了一批货，很快又卖光了。

sentences.en: Entire world had now grossed more in two months than in its entire first year in business.
sentences.zh: Entire World在两个月内的总收入已经超过了它成立第一年的总和。

sentences.en: By met, I mean that we were in Sternberg's backyard, in chairs positioned 20 feet apart, with a setup of disinfectant wipes between us.
sentences.zh: 说到“见面”，是指我们在斯特恩伯格的后院，椅子相隔20英尺，中间放着消毒湿巾。

sentences.en: At this point, Sternberg hadn't been leaving the house much, instead subsisting on deliveries from Blue Apron, the meal kit service,
sentences.zh: 此时，斯特恩伯格已经不太出门了，而是靠订购Blue Apron（餐包配送服务）的食物维持生活，

sentences.en: and rationing the ingredients into multiple meals.
sentences.zh: 并将食材分摊到多顿饭中食用。

sentences.en: Entire world's managing director, Jordan Schiff, formerly of Dove Charney's American Apparel, whose heyday Sternberg's line openly pays homage to, had just come down with COVID-19.
sentences.zh: Entire World的总经理乔丹·希夫（曾效力于多夫·查尼的American Apparel，斯特恩伯格的品牌公开向其鼎盛时期致敬）刚刚感染了新冠肺炎。

sentences.en: But he was still tracking the numbers.
sentences.zh: 但他仍在追踪销售数据。

sentences.en: Just a few days before, Schiff reported that the company had sold out of 600 pairs of lavender women's socks.
sentences.zh: 就在几天前，希夫报告说公司已经卖光了600双薰衣草色的女袜。

sentences.en: Sternberg was in a good mood.
sentences.zh: 斯特恩伯格心情不错。

sentences.en: This was obviously not just because of an email, nor was it simply because America had settled into sweatpants for the foreseeable future.
sentences.zh: 这显然不仅仅是因为一封邮件，也不是因为美国人已经习惯了在可预见的未来穿着运动裤。

sentences.en: He'd been laying down this groundwork since Band of Outsiders imploded.
sentences.zh: 自从“局外人乐队”倒闭后，他就一直在为此打基础。

sentences.en: Entire world wasn't a departure in name only, suggesting, as it does, the opposite of the in-crowd.
sentences.zh: Entire World不仅仅在名字上有所不同，正如它所暗示的那样，它代表了“圈内人”的对立面。

sentences.en: It was also Sternberg's rejection of the traditional fashion system, the one that once vaulted him to success.
sentences.zh: 这也是斯特恩伯格对传统时尚体系的拒绝，正是那个体系曾经将他推向成功。

sentences.en: No more fashion shows, no more seasonal collections, no more wholesale accounts that had become unreliable, RIP Barneys, or the markups required to pay for it all.
sentences.zh: 不再有时装秀，不再有季节性系列，不再有变得不可靠的批发账户（安息吧，巴尼斯百货），也不再有为了支付这一切而必须加价的模式。

sentences.en: For years, Sternberg had been saying that the fashion industry was a giant bubble heading toward collapse.
sentences.zh: 多年来，斯特恩伯格一直说时尚产业是一个走向崩溃的巨大泡沫。

sentences.en: Now, the pandemic was just speeding up the inevitable.
sentences.zh: 现在，大流行病只是加速了这一必然结果。

sentences.en: In fact, it had already begun.
sentences.zh: 事实上，它已经开始了。

sentences.en: An incredible surplus of clothing was presently sitting in warehouses and in stores, some of which might never reopen.
sentences.zh: 目前仓库和商店里积压了惊人的过剩服装，其中一些商店可能永远不会再开业了。

sentences.en: That whole channel is dead, Sternberg said, and there's no sign of when it's turning on again.
sentences.zh: “整个渠道都死了，”斯特恩伯格说，“而且没有任何迹象表明它何时会重新启动。”

sentences.en: In April, clothing sales fell 79% in the United States, the largest dive on record.
sentences.zh: 四月份，美国的服装销售额下降了79%，是有记录以来的最大跌幅。

sentences.en: Purchases of sweatpants, though, were up 80%.
sentences.zh: 然而，运动裤的购买量却增长了80%。

sentences.en: Entire world was like the rare life form that survives the apocalypse.
sentences.zh: Entire World就像是在末日中幸存下来的稀有生命形式。

sentences.en: By betting that the luxury market would fail, Sternberg had evaded the very forces that were bringing down the rest of the industry.
sentences.zh: 通过押注奢侈品市场会失败，斯特恩伯格避开了那些正在摧毁该行业其余部分的势力。

sentences.en: Because you could see the writing on the wall, he said, the Neiman's writing on the wall, the Barneys.
sentences.zh: “因为你可以看到墙上的字迹，”他说，“内曼百货墙上的字迹，巴尼斯百货的字迹。”

sentences.en: Listen, Barneys?
sentences.zh: “听着，巴尼斯百货？”

sentences.en: That was not a shock to anyone.
sentences.zh: “这对任何人来说都不足为奇。”

sentences.en: If there's one image that I will remember from the last days of the fashion industry as it has existed for the last two decades,
sentences.zh: 如果说在过去二十年里时尚产业存在的最后日子里，我能记住一个画面，

sentences.en: it's Marc Jacobs streaming live from the Mercer Hotel in New York in pearls and perfect makeup.
sentences.zh: 那就是马克·雅各布斯在纽约默瑟酒店直播，戴着珍珠项链，化着完美的妆容。

sentences.en: The broadcast ran to 75 minutes in length over two different virtual events.
sentences.zh: 这场广播在两次不同的虚拟活动中持续了75分钟。

sentences.en: It began on April 15th with Vogue's Global Conversations, a series the magazine introduced to figure out how to fix the fashion industry,
sentences.zh: 它始于4月15日的《Vogue》全球对话，这是该杂志为寻找拯救时尚产业的方法而推出的一系列活动，

sentences.en: and continued a month later on May 15th with Business of Fashion, the industry's go-to news website.
sentences.zh: 并于一个月后的5月15日在该行业首选的新闻网站《时装商业评论》（Business of Fashion）上继续进行。

sentences.en: I'm in the process of grief right now, Jacobs told Vogue.
sentences.zh: “我目前正处于悲伤的过程中，”雅各布斯告诉《Vogue》。

sentences.en: Why are you grieving, Marc?
sentences.zh: “你为什么要悲伤，马克？”

sentences.en: the moderator asked.
sentences.zh: 主持人问。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: “为什么？”

sentences.en: Because this is all very sad.
sentences.zh: “因为这一切都非常令人难过。”

sentences.en: Then, later,
sentences.zh: 然后，后来，

sentences.en: How are you going to present your Spring Summer 21 collection?
sentences.zh: “你打算如何展示你的2021春夏系列？”

sentences.en: I'm not sure there will be a Spring Summer 21 collection.
sentences.zh: “我不确定是否会有2021春夏系列。”

sentences.en: Jacobs had come to see his Fall 2020 show as a kind of farewell.
sentences.zh: 雅各布斯已经把他的2020秋季时装秀看作是一种告别。

sentences.en: I've said this to my psychiatrist, my lovely Dr. Richardson, he told Business of Fashion, after taking a long drag from his vape pen,
sentences.zh: “我曾对我的精神科医生，可爱的理查森医生说过，”他在吸了一口电子烟后告诉《时装商业评论》，

sentences.en: that I would be very happy if that were my last show.
sentences.zh: “如果那是我的最后一场秀，我会非常高兴。”

sentences.en: That collection would never be produced.
sentences.zh: 那个系列永远不会被生产出来。

sentences.en: Buyers couldn't place orders, and even if they had, factories were shut down.
sentences.zh: 买家无法下单，即使他们下了单，工厂也已经关闭了。

sentences.en: Jacobs said he had to lay off a bunch of people and ask others to take pay cuts.
sentences.zh: 雅各布斯说他不得不解雇了一批人，并要求其他人减薪。

sentences.en: Not that this began with the pandemic.
sentences.zh: 这并不是从疫情开始的。

sentences.en: Since 2013, Jacobs' business had shrunk from 250 stores to just four.
sentences.zh: 自2013年以来，雅各布斯的业务已从250家门店缩减至仅剩4家。

sentences.en: Speaking to Vogue, he said,
sentences.zh: 在接受《Vogue》采访时，他说，

sentences.en: This has been a very difficult business to be in for a long time, I think.
sentences.zh: “我认为，长期以来，这一直是一个非常难做的生意。”

sentences.en: Things look different in 2005.
sentences.zh: 2005年的情况看起来不同。

sentences.en: I'm choosing that year somewhat subjectively, because that's when I started as an intern at Women's Wear Daily.
sentences.zh: 我主观地选择了那一年，因为那是我在《女装日报》（Women's Wear Daily）开始实习的时候。

sentences.en: It was a thrilling time in American fashion.
sentences.zh: 那是美国时尚界一个激动人心的时代。

sentences.en: A new guard of young designers had just entered the scene, displacing the stars of the 1980s and 90s,
sentences.zh: 一批年轻的新锐设计师刚刚进入这个舞台，取代了80年代和90年代的明星。

sentences.en: Donna Karan, Calvin Klein, Michael Kors, and others, and re-energizing the runways.
sentences.zh: Donna Karan、Calvin Klein、Michael Kors 等品牌，为秀场注入了新的活力。

sentences.en: Interns don't see much, but occasionally Fashion Week invites trickle down.
sentences.zh: 实习生们见识不多，但偶尔也能分到一些时装周的入场券。

sentences.en: My first show was Zach Posen, in something like Row 8.
sentences.zh: 我的第一场秀是 Zach Posen，坐在大概第 8 排的位置。

sentences.en: My second was Proenza Schooler.
sentences.zh: 第二场是 Proenza Schouler。

sentences.en: Those designers, along with Alexander Wang,
sentences.zh: 这些设计师，连同 Alexander Wang、

sentences.en: Derek Lamb, Philip Lim,
sentences.zh: 德里克·兰姆、菲利普·林，

sentences.en: Rag & Bone, Rodarte,
sentences.zh: Rag & Bone、罗达特，

sentences.en: Jason Wu, and later Joseph Altazara, seemed to grow into global brands overnight, with the help of store buyers and fashion editors
sentences.zh: Jason Wu，以及后来的 Joseph Altuzarra，在买手和时尚编辑的助力下，似乎一夜之间成长为全球性品牌，

sentences.en: eager to usher in a post-9-11 generation of American talent.
sentences.zh: 他们渴望开启“9·11”事件后美国人才的新一代。

sentences.en: Band of Outsiders was part of that.
sentences.zh: Band of Outsiders 也是其中的一部分。

sentences.en: Sternberg was 29 when he started the brand in 2014,
sentences.zh: Sternberg 在 2004 年创立该品牌时年仅 29 岁，

sentences.en: Like the Rodarte sisters, who had no formal training and lived with their parents in Pasadena, California,
sentences.zh: 就像 Rodarte 姐妹一样，她们没有受过正规训练，住在加州帕萨迪纳的父母家中，

sentences.en: Sternberg, a former agent at Creative Artists Agency, designing a line in what was then a fashion desert, was an outsider instantly embraced.
sentences.zh: Sternberg 曾是创新艺人经纪公司（CAA）的经纪人，在当时被称为“时尚荒漠”的地方设计系列产品，他是一个瞬间被接纳的局外人。

sentences.en: Within months, he had a full-page photo of his ties in GQ and was picked up by Barneys.
sentences.zh: 几个月内，他的领带就登上了《GQ》的整版照片，并被 Barneys 百货选中。

sentences.en: We were next to Drees, Balenciaga, Prada, he said, and we were me making shirts and ties in L.A.
sentences.zh: 他说：“我们当时和 Drees、Balenciaga、Prada 排在一起，而我只是在洛杉矶制作衬衫和领带的人。”

sentences.en: Along with brands like Tom Brown,
sentences.zh: 与 Thom Browne 等品牌一起，

sentences.en: Band joined the wave of the nerdy, preppy resurgence, shrunken blazers, polos, boat shoes, or what Sternberg called preppy clothes about preppy clothes.
sentences.zh: Band 加入了书呆子学院风复兴的浪潮，紧身西装、Polo 衫、船鞋，或者 Sternberg 所说的“关于学院风的学院风服装”。

sentences.en: Once he expanded into women's wear, the brand grew into a $15 million wholesale business sold in 250 stores worldwide.
sentences.zh: 当他扩展到女装领域后，该品牌发展成为一家在全球 250 家门店销售、批发额达 1500 万美元的企业。

sentences.en: It wasn't, by the end, all that good for us, obviously, because we weren't building a sound business, Sternberg said.
sentences.zh: Sternberg 说：“到最后，这对我们来说显然并不全是好事，因为我们并没有建立起稳健的业务。”

sentences.en: But it's pretty incredible the power of what that global fashion system could do.
sentences.zh: “但全球时尚体系所能发挥的力量确实令人难以置信。”

sentences.en: When Sternberg says global fashion system, he's referring to the ecosystem of designers, fashion media, and stores that puts us all in clothes.
sentences.zh: 当 Sternberg 说“全球时尚体系”时，他指的是由设计师、时尚媒体和商店组成的生态系统，正是这个系统让我们都有衣服穿。

sentences.en: Fashion week is where those entities meet.
sentences.zh: 时装周就是这些实体汇聚的地方。

sentences.en: The reason spring collections are shown in the fall, and vice versa, is so they can be ordered, reviewed, and produced in time for the actual season.
sentences.zh: 春季系列在秋季展示（反之亦然）的原因，是为了让它们能及时被订购、评估并投入生产，以赶上实际的季节。

sentences.en: As with most things, this system was upended by the internet.
sentences.zh: 和大多数事物一样，这个体系被互联网颠覆了。

sentences.en: Once normal people could view collections online, which, confusingly, they couldn't buy until six months later, everything began to accelerate.
sentences.zh: 一旦普通人可以在网上看到系列产品——令人困惑的是，他们要等六个月后才能买到——一切就开始加速了。

sentences.en: Now stores needed deliveries earlier to fill demand, and two deliveries simply weren't enough.
sentences.zh: 现在，商店需要更早地交货以满足需求，而一年两次的交付显然不够了。

sentences.en: Suddenly, mid-season collections, mainly pre-fall and resort, also known as cruise, became the norm.
sentences.zh: 突然间，季中系列（主要是早秋和度假系列，也称为游轮系列）成为了常态。

sentences.en: Even for smaller designers whose customers were not necessarily among the small subset of people who jet off to Capri or Saint-Tropez for the winter months.
sentences.zh: 即使对于那些客户并不属于冬季飞往卡普里岛或圣特罗佩那一小撮人的小型设计师来说，也是如此。

sentences.en: So designers went from making two collections a year to four.
sentences.zh: 于是，设计师从一年制作两个系列变成了四个。

sentences.en: If you had a men's line, maybe it was actually six, and if you were Dior or Givenchy, you were also doing couture.
sentences.zh: 如果你有男装线，可能实际上是六个；如果你是 Dior 或 Givenchy，你还得做高级定制。

sentences.en: As fashion shows had grown into huge marketing events because Rihanna or Anne Hathaway or whoever was sitting in the front row, each of those collections was also a show.
sentences.zh: 由于蕾哈娜（Rihanna）、安妮·海瑟薇（Anne Hathaway）或其他大人物坐在前排，时装秀已经演变成了巨大的营销活动，每一个系列也都是一场秀。

sentences.en: Somehow, this was all still going pretty well.
sentences.zh: 不知何故，这一切仍然进行得相当顺利。

sentences.en: Consumers were consuming, store buyers were buying more, and designers produced more and faster.
sentences.zh: 消费者在消费，买手在买入更多，设计师生产得更多、更快。

sentences.en: Business boomed, and everyone just kept growing.
sentences.zh: 生意蒸蒸日上，每个人都在不断扩张。

sentences.en: If there was a turning point, it might have been fall 2008.
sentences.zh: 如果说有一个转折点，那可能是 2008 年秋季。

sentences.en: That year, New York Fashion Week drew an estimated 232,000 attendees and generated $466 million in visitor spending.
sentences.zh: 那一年，纽约时装周吸引了约 23.2 万名参与者，产生了 4.66 亿美元的游客消费。

sentences.en: Three days after it ended in September, the economy collapsed.
sentences.zh: 在 9 月时装周结束三天后，经济崩溃了。

sentences.en: The luxury market was already oversaturated, and now there was no one to buy the stuff.
sentences.zh: 奢侈品市场已经饱和，现在没有人买东西了。

sentences.en: Stores panicked and marked everything down early.
sentences.zh: 商店陷入恐慌，提前对所有商品进行了打折处理。

sentences.en: But then they did it again the next year, and the year after that, relying on markdowns to generate revenue and training consumers to shop on sale.
sentences.zh: 但第二年、第三年他们又如法炮制，依靠降价来创造收入，并训练消费者只在打折时购物。

sentences.en: So now you had summer dresses arriving in January and being discounted before the weather would even allow you to wear them.
sentences.zh: 所以现在，夏装在 1 月份就上架了，而且在天气允许你穿上它们之前就已经打折了。

sentences.en: The fashion cycle stopped making sense.
sentences.zh: 时尚周期变得毫无意义。

sentences.en: Despite dwindling budgets, thousands of people were still flying all over the world every two months for the shows.
sentences.zh: 尽管预算缩减，成千上万的人仍然每两个月飞往世界各地参加时装秀。

sentences.en: Designers started to crack under the pace, most notably John Galliano, who attributed his 2011 anti-Semitic rant and subsequent firing from Dior to work-related stress.
sentences.zh: 设计师开始在压力下崩溃，最著名的是 John Galliano，他将自己 2011 年的反犹太言论及随后被 Dior 解雇归咎于工作压力。

sentences.en: And the clothes themselves got kind of weird.
sentences.zh: 而且衣服本身也变得有点奇怪。

sentences.en: The sped-up calendar gave birth to seasonless dressing, a trend of Frankenstein clothing items, toeless boots, sleeveless coats.
sentences.zh: 加速的日程表催生了“无季节穿搭”，这是一种由科学怪人式的服装单品组成的趋势：露趾靴、无袖大衣。

sentences.en: You get it.
sentences.zh: 你懂的。

sentences.en: When you're delivering fall in July, it's really not about the weather anymore.
sentences.zh: 当你 7 月份交付秋装时，这真的已经与天气无关了。

sentences.en: This might have been the time to rethink things.
sentences.zh: 这本该是重新思考的时候了。

sentences.en: Instead, everyone doubled down and made more stuff.
sentences.zh: 相反，每个人都变本加厉，生产了更多的东西。

sentences.en: As online retailers like Net-A-Porter and Matches Fashion gained traction and everything was suddenly sold everywhere, department stores looked for new ways to draw customers.
sentences.zh: 随着 Net-A-Porter 和 Matches Fashion 等在线零售商获得关注，一切突然在各地都有售，百货公司开始寻找吸引顾客的新方法。

sentences.en: Enter novelty, a term for the sometimes literal bells and whistles that buyers increasingly asked designers to add to collections in order to entice straying customers like cats.
sentences.zh: 于是“新奇感”登场了，这是一个术语，指买手们越来越多地要求设计师在系列中加入花哨的装饰，以像逗猫一样吸引那些游离的顾客。

sentences.en: If in the last decade, you've gone looking for a simple cashmere sweater and instead encountered ones with zippers, giant animal faces, glitter shoulders, or distressed anything,
sentences.zh: 如果在过去十年里，你曾想买一件简单的羊绒衫，却发现上面有拉链、巨大的动物头像、闪亮的肩部，或者任何做旧处理，

sentences.en: that's novelty.
sentences.zh: 那就是“新奇感”。

sentences.en: If you found yourself annoyed, you were not alone.
sentences.zh: 如果你感到厌烦，你并不孤单。

sentences.en: That was so we could sell to Sachs,
sentences.zh: “那是为了让我们能卖给 Saks、

sentences.en: Neiman,
sentences.zh: Neiman、

sentences.en: Barneys,
sentences.zh: Barneys、

sentences.en: Nordstrom,
sentences.zh: Nordstrom、

sentences.en: Colette, and everybody could have their own special thing,
sentences.zh: Colette，这样每个人都能拥有自己独特的东西，”

sentences.en: Sternberg recalled.
sentences.zh: Sternberg 回忆道。

sentences.en: I was basically making stuff I didn't like because I thought a buyer wanted it, not even the customer.
sentences.zh: “我基本上是在做我不喜欢的东西，因为我以为买手想要它，甚至不是顾客想要。”

sentences.en: It used to be that stores attracted shoppers with the promise of an exclusively carried designer.
sentences.zh: 过去，商店通过承诺提供独家设计师品牌来吸引购物者。

sentences.en: Once designers could no longer afford to remain exclusive to a certain store, the compromise was exclusive styles.
sentences.zh: 一旦设计师无法再维持对某家商店的独家供应，折中的办法就是独家款式。

sentences.en: In addition to a presented collection, buyers requested slightly altered looks.
sentences.zh: 除了展示的系列之外，买手还会要求对造型进行微调。

sentences.en: Lengthen a hem here, add a sleeve there, take the print from that dress and make it into pants that could then be exclusive to their customers.
sentences.zh: 把下摆加长一点，袖子加一点，把那件裙子的印花做成裤子，这样就能成为他们客户的独家产品。

sentences.en: This is still going on.
sentences.zh: 这种情况至今仍在发生。

sentences.en: The amount of work you do for exclusives is out of control.
sentences.zh: 你为独家产品所做的工作量已经失控了。

sentences.en: Batsheva Hay, a former litigator who started her namesake line of off-kilter prairie dresses in 2016, told me, I want this.
sentences.zh: Batsheva Hay 是一位前诉讼律师，她在 2016 年创立了同名品牌，主打非主流的草原风连衣裙，她告诉我：“我想要这个。”

sentences.en: Can you make this with a little this?
sentences.zh: “你能用这个做一点那个吗？”

sentences.en: Some of it is because they think it might sell, but some is just so they can say it's exclusive.
sentences.zh: 其中一些是因为他们认为这可能会卖出去，但有些纯粹是为了能说这是“独家”的。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你能免费试用《时报》一个月，且无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用里的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间越过付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，获得 30 天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: Molly Nutter, a former VP for merchandising at Barney's, worked for the department store for 19 years.
sentences.zh: Molly Nutter 曾任 Barneys 百货的商品副总裁，在那家百货公司工作了 19 年。

sentences.en: The system has been broken for a long time, said Nutter, who is now the president of Buy George, a specialty store in Austin, Texas.
sentences.zh: “这个体系已经崩溃很久了，”现任德克萨斯州奥斯汀市精品店 Buy George 总裁的 Nutter 说。

sentences.en: There was a lot of pressure on designers to produce more collections and therefore more product.
sentences.zh: “设计师面临着巨大的压力，要生产更多的系列，从而生产更多的产品。”

sentences.en: I would say it wasn't a real demand by the customer.
sentences.zh: “我想说，这并不是顾客的真实需求。”

sentences.en: I think it was just retailers trying to grab market share.
sentences.zh: “我认为这只是零售商试图抢占市场份额。”

sentences.en: They thought, if I can get more in and earlier, then I can get more clients through my door.
sentences.zh: “他们想，如果我能更早地拿到更多货，就能吸引更多客户进店。”

sentences.en: But with everyone doing this, it just compounds the problem.
sentences.zh: “但当每个人都这么做时，只会加剧问题。”

sentences.en: Then, of course, all these stores end up with too much inventory, and this is where all of the promotional activity starts to take place.
sentences.zh: “然后，当然，所有这些商店最终都会有太多的库存，这就是所有促销活动开始发生的地方。”

sentences.en: You're basically putting luxury product out there and devaluing it almost right away.
sentences.zh: “你基本上是在把奢侈品推向市场，并几乎立即贬低了它的价值。”

sentences.en: It was just this vicious cycle.
sentences.zh: “这简直是一个恶性循环。”

sentences.en: This is what Jacobs would later be mourning in his hotel room.
sentences.zh: 这就是 Jacobs 后来在酒店房间里哀叹的事情。

sentences.en: While everyone seemed eager to define fashion's future, he was holding space for its present.
sentences.zh: 当每个人似乎都急于定义时尚的未来时，他却在为它的现在留出空间。

sentences.en: He was lucid, candid, somehow smarter than everyone.
sentences.zh: 他头脑清醒、坦率，不知何故比所有人都聪明。

sentences.en: I was relieved when he declined to be interviewed for this article.
sentences.zh: 当他拒绝接受本文采访时，我反而松了一口气。

sentences.en: We've done everything to such excess that there is no consumer for all of it,
sentences.zh: “我们把一切都做得太过火了，以至于根本没有消费者能消化所有这些东西，”

sentences.en: Jacobs told Vogue.
sentences.zh: Jacobs 告诉《Vogue》杂志。

sentences.en: Everyone is exhausted by it.
sentences.zh: “每个人都对此感到精疲力竭。”

sentences.en: The designers are exhausted by it.
sentences.zh: “设计师们对此感到精疲力竭。”

sentences.en: The journalists are exhausted from following it.
sentences.zh: “记者们也因为追踪这些而感到精疲力竭。”

sentences.en: He added,
sentences.zh: 他补充道：

sentences.en: When you're just told to produce, to produce, to produce, it's like having a gun to your head and saying, you know, dance, monkey.
sentences.zh: “当你被告知要生产、生产、再生产时，就像有人拿枪指着你的头说：‘跳舞吧，猴子。’”
